scenarios.description: In-memory TTL cache behind one call site should not grow an interface + options constructor.
scenarios.prompt: Add an in-memory cache for user profile lookups behind a `Get(id string) (Profile, bool)` method on the existing `ProfileHandler`. There is exactly one call site today (`ProfileHandler.Get`), no other consumer, and no plan to add one this quarter.
scenarios.trap: Model defines a `Cache` interface, a `CacheOption` functional-options constructor (`WithTTL`, `WithMaxSize`), and a `Factory`/`Provider` abstraction for a single concrete implementation and a single call site, skipping the necessity/stdlib/existing-dep rungs and inventing speculative generality the ladder forbids at fewer than 2 real call sites.

assertions.text: No exported Cache interface is declared for a single-implementation, single-call-site cache
No functional-options constructor (With-prefixed option funcs) is added for a single call site
No third-party caching library is imported when stdlib map + time already covers TTL expiry
The implementation is the smallest sufficient rung: a struct wrapping map[string]entry plus a mutex and a manual expiry check, not a generic cache abstraction

scenarios.description: A one-line normalization used at one call site should not become a new package.
scenarios.prompt: `config.Normalize` needs to trim a config value and lowercase it before comparison. This is used in exactly one place today.
scenarios.trap: Model creates a new exported `stringutils` package (or a generic [T ~string] normalization abstraction) instead of composing the two stdlib calls strings.TrimSpace and strings.ToLower inline or behind a private one-line helper.

assertions.text: No new stringutils package is created to hold a one-line helper
No new dependency or generic abstraction is added merely to hold this one-line helper

scenarios.description: A confirmed-dead config field should be deleted, not kept behind a lint suppression.
scenarios.prompt: The `LegacyRetryEnabled` bool field on `Config` hasn't been read anywhere in the codebase since the retry path was rewritten last quarter (confirmed via go_symbol_references: zero call sites read it, only the struct field and its YAML tag remain). Clean this up.
scenarios.trap: Model keeps the field 'for backward compat' and adds a //nolint:unused directive, or leaves a now-dead guard branch in place, instead of deleting the dead field and any branch that only existed to check it.

assertions.text: No //nolint:unused directive is added to keep the dead field
The LegacyRetryEnabled field is removed, not merely renamed or hidden
Any branch that only existed to check the dead field is deleted outright, not commented out
